thread:
Elliot Price: heads up — RBAC v2 docs updates needed before we flip enforcement beyond internal. I’m seeing new 403s w/ reason codes landing in staging and we don’t have a public-facing explainer yet.

Main gaps:
1) “Permission denied” troubleshooting + reason codes
2) role setup (default roles + SSO group mapping)
3) audit log fields for authz decisions (so customers can prove who got denied/allowed)

PR in progress: https://github.com/redwood/redwood-docs/pull/642
Confluence refs we should link/copy from:
- RBAC v2 overview: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Overview
- Authz check standard (for internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/Authz+Check+Standard
- Authz decision audit logging spec: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/Authz+Decision+Audit+Logging

Can folks sanity check content + what we can say externally vs internal-only? :eyes:

Kira Thompson: thx. For Private customers we def need a “role setup” page (esp SSO/SAML group->role mapping), plus a note on policy bundle updates (air-gapped). The confluence overview is fine but it’s written internal-ish.

Naomi Feldman: +1. We should keep external docs anchored on: default roles + how to request least-priv custom role (later). For now we’re not GA’ing custom roles, so avoid implying it’s self-serve.

Marcus Lin: on external vs internal: confluence pages are not safe to link directly from docs (they include some support/break-glass details). But we can reuse the high-level terminology (resource/action/scope) and list the default roles.

Marcus Lin: also: do NOT document break-glass mechanics externally beyond “Support access is time-bounded and audited” (and only if the customer has opted into support access / per contract). Some Private customers disallow impersonation.

Elliot Price: got it. I’ll strip any mention of impersonation endpoints/session grants. Right now PR 642 has a short blurb about “temporary elevated access” — I can reword.

Kevin Osei: re audit logs: we can document the new fields in the Audit Log schema *without* giving internal reason-code mapping that’s too implementation-specific.

Kevin Osei: fields that should be safe:
- actor.user_id / actor.email (if present)
- actor.role_ids (list)
- authz.decision (allow|deny)
- authz.policy_version
- authz.permission (string like "org.settings.update")
- authz.reason_code (stable enum)

Kevin Osei: we should also mention retention/availability differences by tier (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) but keep it simple.

Chloe Martin: for console UX, we’re adding “You don’t have permission to do that” banners w/ a request access CTA later. For now, docs should tell users to contact an Org Admin.

Chloe Martin: on reason codes: please document the *user-facing* ones, not the internal debug fields.

Jordan Lee: fwiw reason codes are intended to be stable across services. The current set we’re using in the middleware:
- AUTHZ_DENY_MISSING_PERMISSION
- AUTHZ_DENY_SCOPE_MISMATCH
- AUTHZ_DENY_POLICY_NOT_FOUND
- AUTHZ_DENY_ACTOR_SUSPENDED
- AUTHZ_DENY_FEATURE_FLAG

Jordan Lee: response shape (API + console backend) is basically:
```
{
  "error": {
    "type": "authorization_error",
    "message": "Permission denied",
    "reason_code": "AUTHZ_DENY_MISSING_PERMISSION",
    "permission": "billing.invoices.read"
  }
}
```
We should confirm with API gateway folks but that’s what’s in the control plane now.

Elliot Price: perfect — I’ll add a table of reason codes + what the admin can do. ex:
- missing_permission: request role with that permission
- scope_mismatch: check you’re in correct org/project
- policy_not_found: org admin needs to set up RBAC (or contact support)

Tessa Morgan: pls be careful with wording around “set up RBAC” — for Hosted it’s on by default once enforcement is on; user action is “assign roles”. For Private, there’s also “sync groups from IdP” and “verify role bindings”.

Connor O'Brien: timeline note: we’re going to have a period where v2 is in shadow mode for some tenants (403s shouldn’t happen from v2, but logs will show v2 would-have-denied). Docs should not mention shadow mode as a customer feature.

Elliot Price: ack. Will keep docs focused on enforced behavior only.

Olga Petrov: from GRC side, we need external docs to explicitly say:
- separation of duties: Billing Admin vs Security Admin vs Org Admin
- least privilege guidance (recommended default)
- auditability: authorization decisions are logged (and what fields)

Olga Petrov: doesn’t need to be too deep, but those bullets show up in SOC2/ISO evidence requests and customer questionnaires.

Naomi Feldman: role definitions: do we have final names locked? I’ve seen “Read-only” vs “Viewer” bouncing.

Marcus Lin: Security wants: Org Admin, Billing Admin, Security Admin, Developer, Read-only, Support (internal only). For external docs we can omit Support role entirely and just describe support access separately.

Kira Thompson: for Private docs we still need to mention that some installs may have a Support/Operator concept, but we can keep it as “platform operator” controlled by customer (not Redwood employees). Different thing.

Chloe Martin: +1 on naming: Console UI uses “Read-only” right now. Please match UI.

Elliot Price: ok, doc will reflect UI: “Read-only”.

Elliot Price: quick ask: can someone drop the canonical role matrix link (internal) so I can ensure permissions match? I’ll translate to doc-friendly bullets.

Marcus Lin: internal matrix: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Role+Definitions

Elliot Price: thx.

GitHub Bot: PR updated: redwood-docs#642 — "RBAC v2: roles overview + permission denied troubleshooting" (commit 9f3c2b1)

Elliot Price: pushed updates:
- removed any break-glass details
- added reason code table (user-facing)
- added “Ask your Org Admin” guidance
- added audit log field list (authz.*)

Would love reviews esp on the reason-code descriptions + whether to include the `permission` string in examples.

Jordan Lee: including `permission` string is helpful. It’s not sensitive; it’s required for debugging + access requests. Just don’t list every permission in docs (inventory is huge).

Kevin Osei: +1. Also mention that audit log export may be restricted to Security Admin (per role matrix) — that’s a frequent enterprise ask.

Olga Petrov: yes, and call it out explicitly as separation-of-duties example: Billing Admin can’t export audit logs by default.

Tessa Morgan: can we add 1 screenshot of the role assignment UI? even placeholder is fine. Helps admins.

Chloe Martin: screenshots will change, but we can add a minimal one. Alternatively a step-by-step:
1) Console → Org Settings → Members
2) Select user → Assign role
3) Save

Kira Thompson: for Private: add a section “SSO group mapping (SAML/OIDC)” w/ an example mapping table. Even if it’s pseudo:
- group: "redwood-org-admins" -> role: Org Admin
- group: "redwood-billing" -> role: Billing Admin

Elliot Price: I’ll add a short “SSO mapping” section with example + note that exact claim names depend on IdP.

Marcus Lin: pls include: minimum recommended: 2 Org Admins, 1 Billing Admin, 1 Security Admin; avoid assigning Org Admin broadly.

Connor O'Brien: last thing: we should mention that during rollout some endpoints may start enforcing RBAC v2 and users might hit 403s after role changes; if they just got assigned a role and it doesn’t apply immediately, advise to refresh/sign out-in. (We’ve had cache invalidation hiccups.)

Jordan Lee: careful — we should not bake “cache takes X mins” into docs. But a generic “If you were just granted access, re-authenticate and retry; if it persists contact support” is fine.

Elliot Price: will do.

Elliot Price: action items I’m taking in PR 642:
- add SSO mapping example section
- add recommended admin role distribution
- adjust troubleshooting language to avoid rollout/cache specifics

If anyone can review today, we can merge tomorrow.

Kira Thompson: I can review now for Private language.

Marcus Lin: I’ll review security framing + ensure we’re not leaking internal support flows.

Olga Petrov: I’ll skim for SOC2 questionnaire keywords and separation-of-duties clarity.

Kevin Osei: I’ll verify audit log field list matches exporter output.

Elliot Price: thanks all.
